nodes.summary: The statement that for every strictly increasing sequence $n_0 < n_1 < \cdots$ of natural numbers such that the cardinals $2^{\aleph_{n_k}}$ are strictly increasing in $k$ and $2^{\aleph_{n_0}} > \aleph_\omega$, the partition relation $\sum_k 2^{\aleph_{n_k}} \to (\aleph_\omega)^2_2$ holds: for every set $X$ of cardinality $\sum_k 2^{\aleph_{n_k}}$ and every symmetric colouring of the pairs of elements of $X$ with…
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 1219: a partition relation for sums of powers of two

nodes.summary: For cardinals $\kappa$ and $\mu$, the relation $\kappa \to (\mu)^2_2$ holds if for every set $X$ of cardinality $\kappa$ and every symmetric colouring $c$ of the ordered pairs of elements of $X$ with two colours, there are a subset $H \subseteq X$ of cardinality $\mu$ and a colour $b$ such that $c(x, y) = b$ for all distinct $x, y \in H$.
nodes.title: Partition relation for pairs with two colours

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha = \omega^{\omega^2}$. For every red/blue colouring of the edges of the complete graph on the ordinals less than $\alpha$, that is, every pair of complementary simple graphs (red and blue) on this set, there is a red clique whose order type is $\alpha$ or a blue clique with exactly $3$ elements. In partition notation, $\alpha \to (\alpha, 3)^2$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 591 is true

nodes.summary: The statement that, for $\alpha = \omega^{\omega^2}$, every red/blue colouring of the edges of the complete graph on the ordinals less than $\alpha$ (that is, every pair of complementary simple graphs, red and blue, on this set) has a red clique whose order type is $\alpha$ or a blue clique with exactly $3$ elements. In partition notation, $\alpha \to (\alpha, 3)^2$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 591

nodes.summary: Let $c$ assign a colour in $\gamma$ to each finite subset of a type $I$, and let $n \in \mathbb{N}$. A set $H \subseteq I$ is homogeneous for $c$ with colour $k \in \gamma$ if $c(s) = k$ for every $n$-element subset $s$ of $H$.
nodes.title: Homogeneous set

nodes.summary: For ordinals $\alpha$, $\beta$ and a cardinal $c$, the partition property $\alpha \to (\beta, c)^2$ holds if for every coloring of the edges of the complete graph on the ordinals less than $\alpha$ in red and blue, either some set of vertices whose order type is $\beta$ has all its edges red, or some set of vertices of cardinality exactly $c$ has all its edges blue.
nodes.title: Ordinal–cardinal Ramsey property

nodes.summary: There exist an ordinal $\alpha$ satisfying the partition relation $\alpha \to (\alpha, 3)^2$ and a natural number $n \ge 3$ such that $\alpha$ does not satisfy $\alpha \to (\alpha, n)^2$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 118 fails for ordinals

nodes.summary: The statement that for every ordinal $\alpha$ satisfying the partition relation $\alpha \to (\alpha, 3)^2$ and every natural number $n \ge 3$, the ordinal $\alpha$ also satisfies $\alpha \to (\alpha, n)^2$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 118 for ordinals

inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.
